entries.core_move: Interpret |$H(j\omega)$| as the frequency-dependent amplitude scaling applied by a continuous-time LTI system to sinusoidal inputs, using its variation over $\omega$ to identify which components are attenuated, passed, or amplified.
Interpret $\angle$ $H(j\omega)$ as the frequency-dependent phase shift applied to each sinusoidal input component when using frequency response to characterize LTI filter behavior.

Evaluate low-frequency behavior by examining $H(j\omega)$ as $\omega$ approaches 0 and interpreting its magnitude and phase to decide how an LTI system scales, shifts, passes, or attenuates slowly varying inputs.
Evaluate high-frequency limits of |$H(j\omega)$| and $\angle$ $H(j\omega)$ to predict how an LTI system passes, attenuates, or phase-shifts rapidly varying sinusoidal components.

Identify low-pass behavior in $H(j\omega)$ by comparing its magnitude at low and high frequencies and interpreting strong low-frequency passage with high-frequency attenuation as the system preserving slow sinusoidal components while suppressing rapid ones.

Classify high-pass behavior for an LTI filter from its magnitude response by comparing |$H(j\omega)$| at low and high frequencies and identifying low-frequency attenuation with high-frequency passage.
Classify a filter's passband behavior from its magnitude response by comparing low- and high-frequency gain to decide whether the LTI system is low-pass, high-pass, or neither.
